title: Scheduling Recursive Reasoning in Looped Transformers
abstract: arXiv:2609.36653v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recurrent reasoning models have attracted growing attention for scaling test-time computation, typically by iteratively refining latent states with shared parameters. However, these models apply each learned update with a fixed unit scale, which can be conservative when updates make persistent progress and overly aggressive when they fluctuate, limiting the benefit of additional loops. To understand how the scale should vary along the trajectory, we first analyze the sensitivity of terminal loss to recurrent update scale. We show that its temporal average admits an exact decomposition into persistent-progress and centered-fluctuation contributions. Based on this, we introduce the Trajectory Adaptive Progress-Fluctuation Scheduler (TAPS), which tracks their balance across recurrent updates and adapts the step size online. Theoretically, we establish sufficient conditions under which TAPS reduces expected terminal loss and reaches a target

translated_title: 循环Transformer中递归推理的调度
translated_abstract: 循环推理模型因其在测试时扩展计算的能力而受到越来越多的关注，这类模型通常通过使用共享参数迭代地细化潜在状态来实现。然而，这些模型以固定的单位尺度应用每次学习到的更新，当更新取得持续进展时这可能过于保守，而当更新出现波动时又可能过于激进，从而限制了额外循环带来的收益。为了理解尺度应如何沿轨迹变化，我们首先分析了终端损失对循环更新尺度的敏感性。我们证明了其时间平均可以精确分解为持续进展贡献和中心化波动贡献两部分。基于此，我们提出了轨迹自适应进展-波动调度器，它跟踪循环更新过程中这两种贡献之间的平衡，并在线自适应地调整步长。在理论方面，我们建立了TAPS能够降低期望终端损失并达到目标的充分条件。
tldr: 本文提出了TAPS（轨迹自适应进展-波动调度器），通过将循环更新尺度的时间平均精确分解为持续进展与中心化波动贡献，并在线自适应调整步长，在理论保证下降低循环Transformer递归推理的期望终端损失。
en_tdlr: Proposes TAPS, a trajectory-adaptive scheduler that decomposes the temporal average of recurrent update scale into persistent-progress and centered-fluctuation contributions and adjusts the step size online, with theoretical guarantees of reducing expected terminal loss in looped transformer recursive reasoning.
